subject: General discussion: Best way to visualise tables and dataframes in Shiny

messages.author: fd98f08a6ab27905
messages.subject: General discussion: Best way to visualise tables and dataframes in Shiny
parts:
Hello Shiny enthusiasts,

I was building a new shiny app, when I realised that I make use a lot of GoogleVis Tables and that this might not be the best way.
Especially if you have a lot of reactivity, those tables sometimes unsystematically do not appear.

So I am looking for a more reliable alternative with equal visual niceness, usability (easy to implement) and functionality.

What kind of table solution do you prefer in what situation?

messages.subject: Re: General discussion: Best way to visualise tables and dataframes in Shiny
parts: I also recently switched my app from using Gvis tables to data tables in rCharts.  The only downside to the rCharts version is it can take a while to load if it has more than a few thousand rows (mine had 8 columns and ~15k rows, ended up just cutting it down to the top 1000 rows to speed things up).  However, after the initial load time, the switching between pages and doing searches is instantaneous.

parts:
Thanks to everyone for the great suggestions.

Datatables look very nice, but I have problems to style those output to a certain width or to switch of the search bar and other controls.

The parameter documentation at https://datatables.net/usage/options seem to not include to options.

How do you style up your Datatables?

Am Dienstag, 1. Oktober 2013 21:58:11 UTC+2 schrieb Joe Cheng [RStudio]:
We are adding bindings for datatables to Shiny itself in the next release (0.8.0?). The bindings know how to do server-based pagination, so you should be able to get good performance even for very large tables.
